gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Pioneer DEH-S4220BT needs a separately sold adapter to keep the car's steering-wheel audio controls working, or which file types it plays from a burned CD (AAC, MP3, WAV, WMA) compared with a USB stick (adds FLAC and hi-res WAV).
standout_why: I opened JVC's KD-T920BTS page (rank 5). Its only disc-related text is the K2 upsampling claim, with no disc rules, depth or steering-wheel information. I also opened World Wide Stereo's 2026 guide (a top result). It recommends the Sony MEX-N5300BT, Kenwood KDC-X705 and Kenwood DDX9907XR, but its visible text says nothing about finalized CD-R/RW, 8 cm discs, DualDisc, MP3 CDs or adapters. Its only fit detail is 'Shallow Mount: No' for the DDX9907XR. I couldn't open Crutchfield's cited guide (HTTP 403), Pioneer's US and Canadian product pages (HTTP 429) or the Kenwood manual PDFs (HTTP 404). Crutchfield's Q&A page for the DEH-S4220BT (rank 12) is a likely place for the adapter fact, but I didn't open it, so I score this 1, not 2. My strongest mechanism, the maker's list of discs that won't play, is unsourced because I could only see it in search snippets.
decides: This doesn't change the pick. The three CD receivers ChatGPT showed (Pioneer DEH-S4220BT, Sony MEX-N5300BT, JVC/Kenwood) all play standard CDs. The page should add two install facts. First, budget for a steering-wheel interface if the car has those controls, because the Pioneer is only 'ready' for one with an adapter sold separately. Second, a burned MP3 CD plays but lossless FLAC needs the USB port. Next step: open the official manuals and confirm that CD-Rs must be finalized and that 8 cm discs and DualDiscs aren't supported. If confirmed, that is the stronger 'will my discs play' fact.
